name: seren-memory
description: Gives GitHub Copilot and the user access to the SerenMemory store - search, write, brief, and review the hippocampus's drafts.

serenMemory.endpoint.description: Base URL of the SerenMemory service. Default port 7420 matches SerenMemory's own default.

serenMemory.startCommand.description: Shell command used to start the SerenMemory service when it is not reachable. Application-scoped so workspace settings cannot override it (security: prevents a malicious .vscode/settings.json from injecting a different command).

serenMemory.suppressStartPrompt.description: Suppress the 'service not reachable - start it?' prompt on extension activation. Use this if you intentionally run SerenMemory only for some projects.

serenMemory.bearerTokenHint.markdownDescription:
**Bearer token** is stored securely in the OS keychain, not here.

To set or update it, run the command:

`Seren Memory: Set Bearer Token` (via `Ctrl+Shift+P`)

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_search
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search SerenMemory for relevant past context.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the SerenMemory store for relevant facts, preferences, or context. The main retrieval path - call this BEFORE answering anything that might benefit from past context about the user or project. Returns ranked hits across the requested tiers; short-term is weighted highest (most recent context), long-term gets an evidence-count multiplier so well-established facts outrank one-offs.

n_results.description: Max hits to return after merging and ranking across tiers.

include_long.description: Search long-term (durable facts approved from hippocampus drafts).

include_superseded.description: Include superseded long-term entries (historical 'what the user USED to think').

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_write
languageModelTools.userDescription: Write a memory to the short- or near-term tier.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Store a memory entry in the short-term or near-term tier. Use short-term ('short') for transient facts (session notes, observations); use near-term ('near') for future-tense intents ('bring this up later', 'do X next time'). LONG-TERM CANNOT BE WRITTEN DIRECTLY - long-term is the gated tier, written only when the main model approves a SerenHippocampus draft (see seren_memory_review_draft). To get a fact into long-term immediately, use seren_memory_promote_now after writing to short.

content.description: The memory text. For tier='near' this is the intent statement.

topic.description: Topic label - drives the hippocampus's clustering. Use the same topic for related entries so the hippocampus drafts them together.

tier.description: 'short' for working memory, 'near' for open loops / future intents.

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_brief
languageModelTools.userDescription: Submit a brief that opens the hippocampus's next sleep.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Submit a steering brief. A brief OPENS SerenHippocampus's next sleep and steers the draft it writes: what mattered in this period and which topics to promote vs. ignore. promote_hints and noise_hints are matched against each topic cluster's topic+content when the hippocampus decides what to draft - they ARE the lever for steering what becomes long-term memory. Use them.

summary.description: Free-text summary of what mattered in this period.

promote_hints.description: Topic phrases worth remembering durably. A matching cluster is drafted even from a single entry.

noise_hints.description: Topic phrases that are noise. A matching cluster is not drafted.

completed_intents.description: Near-term intents that look done this period.

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_preserve_verbatim
languageModelTools.userDescription: Flag a short-term entry for verbatim promotion.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Mark a short-term entry for verbatim promotion at SerenHippocampus's next sleep - the hippocampus drafts it as a verbatim operation that keeps the exact phrasing instead of synthesising. Use when the WORDS matter, not just the gist (a specific quote, a precise spec, a verbatim user statement). Also pins the entry so it survives aging until the sleep runs. Like every draft operation, it lands in long-term only when you approve it.

short_id.description: ID of the short-term entry to flag verbatim.

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_promote_now
languageModelTools.userDescription: Promote a short-term entry to long-term immediately.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Immediately move a short-term entry to long-term verbatim, skipping the hippocampus's sleep and draft review entirely. Use when you KNOW a fact is durable and shouldn't wait for the next sleep - for example, after the user explicitly tells you to remember something. This is the only way to put a specific fact into long-term immediately (direct long-term writes are forbidden by design - otherwise long-term is written only by approving hippocampus drafts).

short_id.description: ID of the short-term entry to promote immediately.

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_forget_long
languageModelTools.userDescription: Flag a long-term memory to be purged (the Lacuna gate).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Flag a long-term memory for PURGING. The flag means purge: SerenHippocampus executes it on its next tick, with the cascade and a tombstone that keeps the id and the reason, never the content. Never a surgical delete from here - the Lacuna gate is a FLAG, not a scalpel. Use when the user asks to forget something, or for what must not exist (a pasted secret, PII). This is NOT how a wrong or outdated fact gets corrected: write the corrected fact to short-term and let a draft supersede the old core (the old one stays as demoted history).

long_id.description: ID of the long-term entry to flag.

reason.description: Why this must be purged. Required, and the only thing the tombstone keeps.

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_complete_intent
languageModelTools.userDescription: Mark a near-term intent as acted on.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Mark a near-term intent as ACTED ON (not merely referenced). At the hippocampus's next sleep (its /tidy step) a completed intent leaves the open-loop list and becomes a long-term record. Without this call, intents accumulate forever.

intent_id.description: ID of the near-term entry to mark complete.

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_list_drafts
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the hippocampus's drafts awaiting review.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: The review queue. A draft is what SerenHippocampus proposes after a sleep: a list of operations on long-term (new_core, attach, supersede, verbatim), each reviewed on its own. status=pending is the queue; reviewed is history; closed means the chain has landed and the hippocampus culled it; all is everything. Newest first. Read a draft with seren_memory_get_draft before reviewing it.

status.description: Filter drafts by status. 'all' returns every draft.

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_get_draft
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show one draft with every operation and its verdict.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: One draft with every operation (index, kind, content, topic, target_core_id, rationale) and its verdict so far (status, critique). Also shows cluster_id, attempt, and terminal - terminal=true marks the last permitted attempt in the chain, the only time an approval may carry edited_content. Read this before seren_memory_review_draft.

draft_id.description: ID of the draft to read.

languageModelTools.name: seren_memory_review_draft
languageModelTools.userDescription: Approve or deny each operation in a draft.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Approve or deny a draft's operations, one verdict each. Approving APPLIES the operation now: a new core, a satellite attached to a core (and the core's evidence grows), a supersession (the old core stays, demoted), or a verbatim core. Denying records the critique; the hippocampus redrafts that operation and resubmits it as the next attempt in the chain. A deny needs a critique, and CRITIQUES SHOULD BE SPECIFIC - 'conflates X with Y; separate them' beats 'wrong vibe' - the next attempt is written from them. edited_content on an approval is accepted only on a terminal draft (the last permitted attempt); otherwise deny and let the loop do its job. An operation already decided cannot be decided again (409).

draft_id.description: ID of the draft to review.

decisions.description: One verdict per operation, e.g. [{"op": 0, "verdict": "approve"}, {"op": 1, "verdict": "deny", "critique": "conflates X with Y; separate them"}]. Operations left out stay pending.

op.description: The operation's index in the draft.

verdict.description: approve applies the operation now; deny sends it back with the critique.

critique.description: Required on deny: what to fix. Be concrete - the redraft is written from it.

edited_content.description: On approve, terminal drafts only: your revision, applied instead of the operation's content.

note.description: Optional note recorded with the review.
